items.title: fix(doctor): let SIGTERM/SIGINT stop Doctor during maintenance archiv…
items.summary: fix(doctor): let SIGTERM/SIGINT stop Doctor during maintenance archive preparation (#174898) openclaw doctor --fix could ignore SIGTERM and SIGINT: prepareDoctorMaintenanceArchives awaited the CLI's exit cleanup while that cleanup awaited the running command, so a signal left Bun spinning and made Node exit 13 with an unsettled top-level await. Archive preparation now checks cancellation instead of waiting on its own cleanup; SIGTERM and SIGINT exit promptly (143/130). On current main, doctor --fix with the Gateway running returned actionable contention guidance in 3.7 s on the reporter-like state; the reported 10.4 snapshot loop is still being confirmed with the reporter. Refs #174842

items.title: fix(doctor): usage shows provider "***" for history masked before 202…
items.summary: fix(doctor): usage shows provider "***" for history masked before 2026.10.12 (#174665) Related: #173791 (stops new masking at the source) ## What Problem This Solves Fixes: usage reports show a provider literally named `***` (with real token totals) when transcript history was written before 2026.10.12 by a provider whose runtime headers registered its id as a secret, for example GitHub Copilot's `Openai-Organization: github-copilot`. ## User Impact User impact: after `openclaw doctor --fix` (or the update Doctor pass), historical assistant rows show their real provider again in usage and cost views. Rows Doctor cannot attribute from recorded facts stay `***` and Doctor reports how many. Gateway startup does not run this repair. ## Why This Change Was Made Transcript storage used to redact every registered secret value, and values under 18 characters became `***`. #173791 fixes the producer; this repairs existing history through the Doctor owner that already normalizes historical transcripts. - **Same pass, no new module.** A second transform in the historical-transcript Doctor pass reuses its batching, resumable cursor, pre-repair backup, stopped-writer and agent-lease checks, source revalidation and archive walking. No schema change: the cursor JSON gains `version: 2` and a `scope`. - **Attribution from recorded facts only.** A row is rewritten only when the same session's unmasked trajectory runtime events record exactly one provider for the row's model. `***` is not always one provider, so there is no hard-coded mapping. Ambiguous and unrecorded rows stay `***`. - **Only `message.provider` changes.** Every other byte of the event is preserved (asserted in tests). No indexed fact (search text, tree links, active events, context eligibility) holds a provider, so these rewrites skip the session index rebuild; the transcript store owner gains an `indexUnchanged` rewrite option for that. - **Undo record instead of a full backup.** Every restored provider was `***`, so Doctor records the restored rows (`historical-transcript-masked-provider-restored-v1`) in the same transaction as each rewrite instead of copying the whole database. Directive edits still take the full pre-repair backup. - **No repeat integrity check.** When the agent schema is already current and converged, the pass skips the schema-maintenance step that re-verifies the whole database; Doctor's schema steps own that check. - **Runs once.** Completed version 1 installs reopen the pass once for this repair alone (directives are not reparsed); later runs short-circuit on the cursor. An interrupted version 1 cursor restarts both idempotent transforms from the start so no session is skipped. - **Cheap detection, one scan.** Plain rows use an `instr` prefilter on `event_json`. Compressed rows always carry a navigation projection that keeps `message.provider`, so only matching compressed rows are decoded. Candidate sessions come from one rowid-order scan; the previous index-ordered `DISTINCT` listing fetched every row out of order (19.2s vs 12.5s cold on a 1.4 GB database), which also speeds up the existing directive pass. With the writer stopped, the preflight no longer scans; the pass scans once. - The Doctor summary line is now "Repaired historical transcripts in …" because it counts both repairs; a separate line reports restored provider rows. Known gap: `session_transcript_cold_archives` is not scanned, which matches the existing directive pass. A Doctor run that upgrades the agent schema postpones this pass to the next Doctor run (existing behavior from #172390); the E2E on a v27 copy showed exactly that. ## Evidence **Focused tests** (`state-migrations.transcript-directives*`, media-persistence bounded/canonical-archives, doctor transcript labels): 71/71 pass. The original four masked-provider tests fail on the base commit and pass with the fix; the suite now has six. It covers masked identity, zstd and archived rows; a multi-provider session resolved by model; an ambiguous session and an unrecorded session left masked and reported; a completed v1 cursor reopened once without reparsing directives; an idempotent second run; and refusal while an agent database writer lease is held. oxfmt and type-aware oxlint are clean on changed files. **Real `openclaw doctor --fix` on a copy of an affected install** (built CLI, isolated state dir, profile and port, `OPENCLAW_SERVICE_REPAIR_POLICY=external`; the live gateway was not touched): | | Before | After Doctor | |---|---|---| | `sessions.usage` rows with provider `***` | 773 msgs, ~127.5M tokens across 5 sessions | 1 msg (session with no trajectory record) | | Same rows as `github-copilot` | 0 | 772, identical token totals | | Doctor output | — | `Restored masked provider on 772 historical transcript row(s)…`, `Left 1 … row(s) with masked provider "***"…` | The same run on the merged head (`main` now at agent schema v28) upgraded the copy on the first Doctor run and restored the rows on the second, with identical `sessions.usage` results. Tests also cover a session needing both repairs (full backup and index rebuild still happen; mutation-checked) and an interrupted v1 cursor restarting from the first session. Starting an isolated Gateway on the unrepaired copy left the cursor at version 1, so startup does not run the repair. **Latest-stable upgrade (v2026.10.4 → this PR)**: real affected-install history upgraded by stable Doctor (v23 → v24), then this PR's Doctor (v24 → v28, repair on the next run): 95 providers restored with identical `sessions.usage` token totals, 1 unrecorded row left `***`, provider-masked transcript content digest unchanged by the repair, stable-set settings retained. Details: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/174665#issuecomment-6227645996 **Performance** (this pass in-process on the same 1.4 GB copy, from maintenance lease to done): | Case | Before | After | |---|---|---| | First repair (772 rows, 4 sessions), warm cache | ~26s, plus a separate preflight scan | 3.0s | | Nothing to repair, warm cache | 11–25s (maintenance integrity check) | 0.84s | | Already complete | 39–171 ms | 62 ms | | First repair, cold page cache | — | 21s, nearly all reading the table from disk | Built-CLI `openclaw doctor --fix` on the copy still restores 772 rows, leaves 1, and prints no backup line; the largest session rewrite transaction dropped from 2.3–4.5s to 1.4s. Whole-Doctor wall time on this database is 80–180s regardless of this pass and too noisy to isolate it. Co-authored-by: Ayaan Zaidi
